procedure: 1. Image point of a track point: the centre of its SAM box. Camera 2 looks down almost vertically and the calibration pairs are vehicle fronts read by hand, so the box centre is the point on the vehicle's centre line least affected by heading; the box bottom-centre (the contact point used for an oblique camera) would sit at the front or the rear depending on direction.

2. Ground point: the homography of the procedure above, giving ADR-017 grid metres, then the rotation by the world model's bearing into its junction frame. Its error: the ground error of 2 px of image error at that point (Homography.ground_error_at), combined in quadrature with the calibration's median held-out error.

3. Lane: the world-model lane polygon that contains the ground point, if exactly one does; otherwise 'outside_lanes' (none, e.g. inside the junction) or 'ambiguous' (several). A lane-associated point whose distance to its polygon's edge is below its ground error is also marked near_lane_boundary.

4. Reference: every NGSIM vehicle present at the synced tick, its centre being its published front centre moved back by half its published length along its heading (ngsim.kinematics, previous tick), in the same junction frame, with its own lane by the same polygons.
5. Heading and speed of each reference: ngsim.kinematics (previous tick), as step 4 uses it for the centre, turned into the junction frame.

6. Residual: camera point minus reference centre, resolved along (positive ahead) and across (positive to the right) the reference vehicle's own heading, for every point: in or out of lanes and in the junction box. No arm axis.

7. Pairing (camera_gate_v3.pair_tracks): a track-vehicle option exists when the vehicle lies within 3.0 m across and 8.0 m along the track's point in at least 5 frames, and those frames are at least 70% of the track's frames with any vehicle within both windows. Its cost is the median over those frames of (across / 1.6)^2 + (along / 8.0)^2. Options are taken cheapest first (ties by track id, then vehicle id); a track takes one vehicle, and a vehicle takes another track only on frames it has not taken. The counted points are the option's frames.

8. Region of a counted point (camera_gate_v3.region_of), by its reference centre: approach or departure if inside exactly one approach or exit lane polygon; junction_interior if in no lane and inside the box the four stop lines bound; otherwise unknown.

inclusion_and_exclusion.included: every counted point of every paired track: in lanes, outside lanes, in the junction box, at track ends, and boxes touching the image edge
excluded: reference vehicles without a heading (never moved), as v1/v2
frames of a paired track whose vehicle lies beyond the windows (3.0 m across, 8.0 m along): not counted, as v1/v2's 3.0 m radius did not count them; their number is reported (window_excluded_points)

metrics.B_point_lane_agreement: counted points whose camera lane equals the reference lane / counted points where both have a lane
metrics.C_track_lane_agreement: paired tracks whose most frequent camera lane equals their most frequent reference lane / paired tracks with at least 3 counted points where both have a lane
metrics.D_across_heading_p90_m: 90th percentile (numpy, linear interpolation) of |across| over all counted points
metrics.J_across_heading_p90_m: the same over counted points in the junction box, with J_points and J_tracks

all_of: D_across_heading_p90_m <= 1.5 (half the narrowest world-model lane, 3.0 m)
J_across_heading_p90_m <= 1.5 when the junction box has at least 50 counted points from at least 3 tracks; with fewer it is reported as not judged and does not decide
go_rule.regions: the overall D always decides; no region's figure replaces it

consequences.go: The camera tracks enter the world model as a separate camera layer: each entity labelled camera-derived (SAM 3.1 output through the camera 2 calibration, approximated), with its lane or an explicit unknown, its ground error and this gate's measured agreement; NGSIM-derived entities stay as they are and are never merged with them. Only lane-level quantities are derived from the camera (which lane, presence, speed); along-road quantities (stop-line crossings, queue lengths) are not, because ADR-018 still rejects the calibration for along-road distances. The evidence bundle then carries camera items, so Muse can cite them.
consequences.no_go: No camera entity enters the world model; every claim that the camera feeds it is withdrawn, and the SAM step is described as a perception probe with its measured precision and recall. The orchestrated run says its world model comes from the NGSIM trajectories only.

limitations: One 30 s excerpt of one camera. The thresholds are pass/fail rules on this sample, not population estimates.
The corrections were derived from gate v2's data; only this excerpt tests them.
Pairing by a cost that weighs across distance favours small lateral errors; v1/v2's pairing is reported beside it for that reason.
Stopped vehicles show an along-road offset the diagnosis could not explain; along-road quantities stay out of the world model (ADR-018).
The reference is itself approximated: NGSIM states about 2 ft across the road and 4 ft along it.
SAM recall (0.28) is not tested here: the gate asks whether the vehicles SAM does track can be placed in lanes, not whether it tracks every vehicle. Camera-derived counts remain lower bounds.
Masks are not used; boxes are.
D is a percentile over points, so a stationary track (up to 300 points in 30 s) weighs as much as many moving ones: one stationary track that disagrees with NGSIM can decide it, as on v1's data.

A stationary track may be paired with the next car in its own lane (about one car length along) when its own NGSIM vehicle covers less than 70% of the track's frames; its lateral error is unaffected, but the along statistics of stopped vehicles then do not describe one vehicle.
